doc.agentStatus_desc: Real-time agent state indicator (thinking / running / waiting)
doc.agentstatus_a11y_1: The root element has role=status and aria-live=polite, announcing state changes to screen readers.
doc.agentstatus_a11y_2: The indicator icon/dot is aria-hidden; the text label (or aria-label) carries the meaning.
doc.agentstatus_choice_streaming: Stream text output as the model generates it
doc.agentstatus_choice_thought: Show a structured log of past reasoning steps
doc.agentstatus_content_guidelines_1: Use the `message` prop to describe what the agent is doing (e.g., "Searching the web…") rather than relying on the generic status label.
doc.agentstatus_content_guidelines_2: Pair with AgentStatus `done` after a completed action rather than leaving it in `running` — this confirms completion to the user.
doc.agentstatus_design_intent: Designed for agentic interfaces where users need to know at a glance whether the AI is actively processing. The compact indicator can appear inline next to a prompt input, in a chat header, or embedded in a status bar.
doc.agentstatus_i18n_desc: Default status labels are sourced from the `form` namespace (`agent_status.*`). Override with the `message` prop for context-specific text.
doc.agentstatus_intro: AgentStatus displays the current state of an AI agent as a compact animated indicator. It complements ThoughtProcess (a historical log) with a live presence signal — idle, thinking, running, waiting, done, or error.
doc.agentstatus_kb_tab: Tab to focus the element (non-interactive by default).
doc.agentstatus_motion_desc: The thinking state pulses with a scale+opacity animation; running spins a ring. Both respect prefers-reduced-motion.
doc.agentstatus_practice_1: Use size=sm inside dense UIs like chat bubbles; size=lg for dedicated status panels.
doc.agentstatus_practice_2: Reset to idle or done after completion — avoid leaving the component stuck in running state.
doc.agentstatus_responsive: AgentStatus is inline and adapts to any container. The size prop controls visual weight for different layout contexts.
doc.agentstatus_scenario_1_desc: Show in the chat header while the model is generating a response, replacing it with done when finished.
doc.agentstatus_scenario_2_desc: Cycle through running → waiting → running as each tool call dispatches and awaits a result.
doc.aifeedback_a11y_1: Each button carries a descriptive aria-label sourced from i18n keys.
doc.aifeedback_a11y_2: aria-pressed reflects the current selection state for screen readers.
doc.aifeedback_a11y_3: The divider between feedback and regenerate is aria-hidden.
doc.aifeedback_a11y_4: All interactive elements are keyboard-reachable and show :focus-visible outlines.
doc.aifeedback_choice_rate: Rate an AI response as helpful or not helpful
doc.aifeedback_choice_regen: Request a fresh response from the model
doc.aifeedback_design_intent: Inline feedback signals let users rate individual AI responses without disrupting the reading flow. The compact icon-button layout keeps the UI uncluttered while staying accessible via keyboard and screen readers.
doc.aifeedback_guideline_1: Do not add text labels next to the icon buttons — rely on aria-label for accessibility.
doc.aifeedback_guideline_2: Show a brief confirmation message (e.g. "Thanks for your feedback!") in the parent, not inside this component.
doc.aifeedback_i18n_desc: Each button carries a descriptive aria-label sourced from i18n keys.
doc.aifeedback_intro: AIResponseFeedback provides thumbs-up/down feedback controls and an optional regenerate button for rating AI-generated responses. It supports both controlled and uncontrolled usage, toggling feedback off when the same button is clicked twice.
doc.aifeedback_motion_desc: Button state transitions (hover/active/selected) use the --wim-duration-fast token for immediate tactile feedback.
doc.aifeedback_practice_1: Keep the component disabled while a response is still streaming to prevent premature feedback.
doc.aifeedback_practice_2: Persist the feedback value to your backend on selection, not on unmount.
doc.aifeedback_practice_3: Use the controlled feedback prop when the parent needs to reset state (e.g. on regenerate).
doc.aifeedback_responsive: AIResponseFeedback is inline and adapts to its container width. On narrow containers, the compact icon-only layout already fits without adjustment.
doc.aifeedback_scenario_chat: Chat interface: Render below each assistant message bubble to collect per-message quality signals.
doc.aifeedback_scenario_search: Search result ranking: Track thumbs-up rates to feed into RLHF pipelines or A/B testing metrics.
doc.aifeedback_scenario_summary: Document summarisation: Let users mark the summary as helpful or request a revised version via regenerate.
doc.artifactsoverlay_a11y: The overlay is a modal-like region. Focus is trapped when open and restored on close.
doc.artifactsoverlay_best_practice_1: Provide a clear way to close the overlay and return to the chat context.
doc.artifactsoverlay_best_practice_2: Use the fullscreen toggle for complex code or large diagrams to improve readability.
doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_code: Displaying long code files or technical specs
doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_doc: Rendering detailed analysis reports or documents
doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_edit: Use when allowing users to edit code or text in a dedicated side-by-side or overlaid editor view.
doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_preview: Use for full-screen previews of documents or visualizations that require more space than the chat bubble allows.
doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_viz: Showing large data visualizations or graphs
doc.artifactsoverlay_content_guidelines: Keep the title clear and descriptive. Use the actions area for primary operations like Save, Copy, or Download.
doc.artifactsoverlay_design_intent: Derived from the need to separate transient chat messages from persistent, high-value content like code or documents. It slides over the main view to provide a focused reading and interaction space.
doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_1: Typically slides in from the right to complement the main view.
doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_2: Use the showFullscreenToggle for content that needs maximum horizontal space.
doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_3: Often contains a MarkdownRenderer, InteractiveGraph, or CodeDiffViewer.
doc.artifactsoverlay_i18n: All labels, titles, and button text are fully localizable via the consumer.
doc.artifactsoverlay_intro: ArtifactsOverlay is a specialized side-panel for displaying large AI-generated content (Artifacts) without interrupting the main chat context.
doc.artifactsoverlay_keyboard: Escape key closes the overlay. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through internal actions.
doc.artifactsoverlay_motion: Slides in from the right edge with a smooth transition. Fullscreen mode uses a scale-and-fade transition.
doc.artifactsoverlay_responsive: The overlay width is responsive (min 600px on desktop, full-width on mobile). Fullscreen mode allows it to cover the entire viewport regardless of screen size.
doc.artifactsoverlay_scenarios: Commonly used in AI coding assistants to show proposed file changes or in research tools to show generated reports.
doc.codeblock_a11y_1: The copy button has a descriptive aria-label which updates when the content is successfully copied.
doc.codeblock_a11y_2: The code content is wrapped in a <pre> and <code> tag for semantic correctness.
doc.codeblock_a11y_3: Line numbers are user-select: none to prevent them from being included in manual text selections.
doc.codeblock_a11y_4: All buttons are focusable and support keyboard activation.
doc.codeblock_design_intent: In AI interfaces, code snippets are frequent and often lengthy. CodeBlock standardizes their presentation, ensuring consistent typography (monospaced) and providing essential utilities like copy-pasting. The collapsible feature allows users to scan the surrounding conversation without being forced to scroll through long blocks of code.
doc.codeblock_guideline_1: Always specify the language prop to display the correct language label and provide accessibility hints.
doc.codeblock_guideline_2: Use showLineNumbers for multi-line snippets where line-specific discussion might occur.
doc.codeblock_guideline_3: Keep maxLines at a reasonable height (e.g., 10-15 lines) when isCollapsible is true.
doc.codeblock_i18n_desc: Labels for the "Copy" and "Expand/Collapse" actions are localized via the form namespace.
doc.codeblock_intro: CodeBlock provides a robust container for displaying code snippets with optional line numbering and a built-in "Copy to Clipboard" utility. It supports a collapsible mode to keep long snippets from overwhelming the page layout.
doc.codeblock_kb_arrows: Scroll the code content horizontally if needed.
doc.codeblock_kb_tab: Navigate between the Copy button, Expand/Collapse toggle, and the code content scroll area.
doc.codeblock_motion_desc: Expand/collapse transitions use CSS Grid animations with the --wim-duration-fast token. The chevron icon rotates 180 degrees to indicate state change.
doc.codeblock_practice_1: Disable the copy button if the code is empty or if the feature is not applicable to the context.
doc.codeblock_practice_2: Use the onCopy callback to trigger analytics or custom toast notifications.
doc.codeblock_practice_3: Ensure the background color of the CodeBlock contrasts well with the surrounding application background.
doc.codeblock_responsive: The CodeBlock container fills the width of its parent and provides horizontal scrolling for long lines. On narrow viewports, it's recommended to use the collapsible mode to save vertical space.
doc.codeblock_scenario_1_desc: Displaying code suggestions or fixes provided by an AI assistant.
doc.codeblock_scenario_2_desc: Rendering code examples with line numbers for easy reference.
doc.codeblock_scenario_3_desc: Using the collapsible mode to show truncated stack traces or logs.
doc.codediff_a11y_1: Apply and Reject buttons carry descriptive visible labels and are keyboard-reachable.
doc.codediff_a11y_2: Line number columns are aria-hidden to avoid repetitive screen-reader output.
doc.codediff_a11y_3: The copy button label changes to Copied! after activation and reverts after 2s.
doc.codediff_a11y_4: View-toggle buttons use aria-pressed to reflect the active view for assistive technology.
doc.codediff_content_guidelines_1: Add an explanatory message above the component when AI is proposing the change so users understand context before reviewing.
doc.codediff_content_guidelines_2: Use `filename` when the path helps orient the reviewer. Omit it for anonymous snippets.
doc.codediff_design_intent: Designed for agentic coding interfaces where AI proposes code changes the user must review. The split view mirrors git diff; the unified view offers a compact single-pane alternative. Below 640 px the view automatically switches to unified.
doc.codediff_i18n_desc: Apply, Reject, Copy, and view-toggle labels are sourced from the `form` namespace and fully localizable.
doc.codediff_intro: CodeDiffViewer displays before/after code changes in git-diff style with line-level highlighting. It supports split and unified views, and can expose Apply/Reject actions for AI-assisted code editing workflows.
doc.codediff_kb_tab: Move focus between Apply, Reject, Copy, and view-toggle buttons.
doc.codediff_motion_desc: No animations. Visual weight comes from background-color highlights on added/removed lines, not motion.
doc.codediff_practice_1: Provide `onApply`/`onReject` callbacks when the diff represents a proposed change the user needs to act on.
doc.codediff_practice_2: Prefer `filename` over bare `language` to give reviewers file context at a glance.
doc.codediff_responsive: Below 640 px the component switches automatically from split to unified view. The header wraps with flex-wrap, so action buttons remain reachable on narrow screens.
doc.codediff_scenario_1_desc: AI suggests file modifications; CodeDiffViewer lets the user inspect and apply changes in one click.
doc.codediff_scenario_2_desc: Surface key hunks from a pull request diff alongside an AI summary.
doc.interactivegraph_a11y: The graph canvas is zoomable via keyboard (+/- keys). Nodes can be navigated and selected using arrow keys.
doc.interactivegraph_best_practice_1: Provide a 'Recenter' or 'Fit to View' button for large graphs to help users re-orient.
doc.interactivegraph_best_practice_2: Use different node shapes or border styles to indicate different node categories.
doc.interactivegraph_choice_agent: Showing interactions between different AI agents
doc.interactivegraph_choice_mapping: Mapping out multi-step agent workflows or state machine transitions visually.
doc.interactivegraph_choice_rag: Visualizing RAG source clusters and retrieval paths
doc.interactivegraph_choice_state: Visualizing state machines or complex decision trees
doc.interactivegraph_choice_viz: Visualizing complex relationships, such as RAG knowledge graphs or hierarchical data structures.
doc.interactivegraph_content_guidelines: Ensure node labels are concise. Use color coding sparingly to distinguish between different types of nodes or states.
doc.interactivegraph_design_intent: Complex AI processes like retrieval or multi-agent orchestration are easier to understand visually. InteractiveGraph provides a performant, zoomable canvas that follows WIM design tokens.
doc.interactivegraph_guideline_1: Allow users to zoom and pan to explore dense networks.
doc.interactivegraph_guideline_2: Nodes use WIM surface tokens and shadows to maintain visual hierarchy.
doc.interactivegraph_guideline_3: Use in large areas or within an ArtifactsOverlay to provide enough room for exploration.
doc.interactivegraph_i18n: Node content and tooltips are provided by the data source and support full localization.
doc.interactivegraph_intro: InteractiveGraph provides a canvas for visualizing node-based data. Ideal for RAG knowledge bases, agent workflows, or state machines.
doc.interactivegraph_keyboard: Use arrow keys to pan. Use +/- to zoom. Enter to select the focused node.
doc.interactivegraph_motion: Nodes and edges animate smoothly when the layout changes. Zoom and pan interactions use standard easing.
doc.interactivegraph_responsive: The graph container fills the available space. On mobile, users can use pinch-to-zoom and touch-drag to navigate.
doc.interactivegraph_scenarios: Ideal for showing how an AI agent retrieved information from a vector database or how a complex logic chain was executed.
doc.markdownrenderer_a11y: Generates semantic HTML tags from the markdown (`#` is `h1`). `baseLevel` changes only the Title size, not the heading outline.
doc.markdownrenderer_best_practice_1: Use semantic headings (H1, H2, H3) to structure long AI responses. When the markdown sits under a page or panel title, pass `baseLevel` so those headings do not outgrow it.
doc.markdownrenderer_best_practice_2: Incorporate CodeBlocks for any technical snippets to ensure proper formatting and copy functionality.
doc.markdownrenderer_choice_docs: Rendering technical documentation or README files
doc.markdownrenderer_choice_rich: When support for tables and complex lists is required
doc.markdownrenderer_content_guidelines: Follow standard Markdown syntax. Ensure that headings are used hierarchically for better accessibility.
doc.markdownrenderer_design_intent: In AI applications, LLM responses are often in Markdown. MarkdownRenderer ensures these responses look like native part of the WIM ecosystem, using semantic Title, Text, and CodeBlock components.
doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_1: Heading sizes follow Title, starting at `baseLevel` (default `2xl`). HTML tags still match the markdown.
doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_2: Automatically uses the WIM CodeBlock component to render code snippets.
doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_3: For very long content, consider wrapping this in a ScrollArea or using it inside an ArtifactsOverlay.
doc.markdownrenderer_i18n: Content is rendered as-is. All wrapper components (like CodeBlock) use localized strings.
doc.markdownrenderer_intro: MarkdownRenderer converts a markdown string into WIM UI components. It uses react-markdown under the hood and applies WIM's typography system.
doc.markdownrenderer_keyboard: Standard browser text selection and keyboard navigation for links and code blocks.
doc.markdownrenderer_motion: No specific animations for static text. In StreamingText, new content appears with a subtle fade.
doc.markdownrenderer_responsive: MarkdownRenderer fills the width of its parent. Components like CodeBlock and Tables handle their own internal horizontal scrolling to prevent layout breaking on small screens.
doc.markdownrenderer_scenarios: Used in chat bubbles, documentation pages, or within Artifacts to render formatted AI output.
doc.modelselector_a11y_1: The trigger exposes aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and aria-controls; the list uses role="listbox" with role="option" items.
doc.modelselector_a11y_2: Arrow keys move the active option and aria-activedescendant tracks it for screen readers.
doc.modelselector_a11y_3: Disabled models carry aria-disabled and cannot be selected by pointer or keyboard.
doc.modelselector_choice_combobox: A long, searchable list of options
doc.modelselector_choice_select: A plain single-choice dropdown without metadata
doc.modelselector_choice_self: Switching models with visible cost and context metadata
doc.modelselector_content_guidelines_1: Keep model names short and recognizable; move the provider into the description line.
doc.modelselector_content_guidelines_2: Format context length compactly (e.g. 128K) and price per 1M tokens so numbers stay scannable.
doc.modelselector_design_intent: Choosing a model is a decision made on trade-offs: capability, context length, and cost. ModelSelector puts those numbers next to each name so the choice is informed rather than guessed.
doc.modelselector_i18n_desc: All built-in meta text (placeholder and the Context/In/Out prefixes) is overridable through the labels prop; model names and prices come from your data.
doc.modelselector_intro: ModelSelector is a dropdown for switching between AI models, surfacing the metadata that matters when choosing one — context window size and per-token pricing.
doc.modelselector_kb_nav: Move between models, skipping disabled ones
doc.modelselector_kb_open: Open the dropdown and focus the current model
doc.modelselector_kb_select: Select the active model, or close without changing
doc.modelselector_motion_desc: The dropdown opens with a short scale-and-fade transition; the chevron rotates 180° to signal the open state.
doc.modelselector_practice_1: Persist the selected model per conversation so switching does not affect existing threads.
doc.modelselector_practice_2: Disable rather than hide deprecated models so links and history remain understandable.
doc.modelselector_practice_3: Hide the pricing row in consumer apps where cost is abstracted away from the user.
doc.modelselector_responsive: The trigger sizes to its content and the dropdown matches the trigger width; set fullWidth to fill a narrow sidebar or mobile sheet.
doc.modelselector_scenario_1_desc: Placed next to the prompt input so users can switch models before sending a message.
doc.modelselector_scenario_2_desc: Used as the default-model picker where pricing and context help teams pick a sensible default.
doc.promptinput_a11y_1: The text area is associated with a label or carries an aria-label.
doc.promptinput_a11y_2: Submit and Attach buttons are focusable and have descriptive labels.
doc.promptinput_a11y_3: Character count and error messages are announced via aria-live.
doc.promptinput_choice_self: Single-turn or multi-turn chat interfaces where users input instructions.
doc.promptinput_guideline_1: Use the placeholder to give examples of effective prompts.
doc.promptinput_guideline_2: Enable showAttach if the model supports file or image grounding.
doc.promptinput_guideline_3: Use fullWidth when the input is the primary action at the bottom of the screen.
doc.promptinput_intro: PromptInput provides a versatile text area optimized for AI prompting, featuring auto-resizing, attachment support, and a dedicated submit action. It handles keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to submit) out of the box.
doc.promptinput_kb_attach: Trigger the file selection dialog (if focused).
doc.promptinput_motion_desc: The container height animates smoothly as text wraps, using standard easing tokens.
doc.promptinput_practice_1: Pair with a character counter for models with strict token limits.
doc.promptinput_practice_2: Provide clear error messages if the input is too long or contains invalid characters.
doc.promptinput_practice_3: Disable the submit button while the AI is already generating a response.
doc.promptinput_responsive: The input container fills the available width. On small screens, the action buttons remain accessible within the input area.
doc.promptinput_scenario_1: Conversational assistant where users type long queries.
doc.promptinput_scenario_2: Image generation tool where users provide detailed descriptive prompts.
doc.promptinput_scenario_3: Data analysis tool where users upload CSV files via the attach button.
doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_1: When rendered as a link, the accessible name comes from the aria-label (title or numbered label).
doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_2: The external link icon is aria-hidden — the rel="noopener noreferrer" and target="_blank" attributes are set automatically.
doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_3: The index badge is aria-hidden so screen readers skip the number and read the full title instead.
doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_1: Limit to 5–6 visible citations; additional sources can be hidden behind a "Show more" toggle.
doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_2: Always provide a title. If no URL is available, omit the url prop rather than passing an empty string.
doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_3: Use the index prop only when you also annotate the prose with matching [n] markers.
doc.sourcecitation_choice_list: Show one or more cited sources below an AI response
doc.sourcecitation_choice_table: Full bibliography or paginated source list
doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_1: Keep titles concise — they are truncated with an ellipsis at the card width.
doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_2: Descriptions should be a single excerpt sentence (≤ 2 lines). Avoid full paragraphs.
doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_3: Domain is auto-derived from the URL. Override only when the hostname is ambiguous.
doc.sourcecitation_design_intent: Grounding AI responses in verifiable sources is essential for trust. The compact card layout makes citations scannable without overwhelming the answer text. The numeric index badge ties each card back to inline citation markers in the prose.
doc.sourcecitation_i18n_desc: The aria-label for numbered citations uses the form namespace key source_citation.source_label (interpolated with index).
doc.sourcecitation_intro: SourceCitation displays a single cited reference — title, domain, and optional description — as a compact card. When a URL is provided it becomes a focusable link that opens in a new tab. Use SourceCitationList to render multiple sources as a wrapping grid.
doc.sourcecitation_keyboard_enter: Open the source URL in a new tab
doc.sourcecitation_keyboard_tab: Move focus to the next citation card (when rendered as a link)
doc.sourcecitation_motion_desc: Hover transitions on the link card use --wim-duration-fast for border-color and background changes, keeping the interaction snappy.
doc.sourcecitation_responsive_desc: SourceCitationList uses flex-wrap so cards reflow naturally on narrow containers. Each SourceCitation card has a max-width to keep it readable at any viewport.
doc.sourcecitation_scenario_assistant: Research assistant: Link academic papers or web pages that the model consulted.
doc.sourcecitation_scenario_rag: RAG responses: Attach retrieved document chunks as citations below the answer.
doc.sourcecitation_scenario_wiki: Internal knowledge base: Surface internal wiki pages as non-link citation cards (no URL).
doc.streamingtext_a11y_1: The content is updated in an aria-live="polite" region (managed internally).
doc.streamingtext_a11y_2: Markdown headings and lists are rendered with correct semantic tags.
doc.streamingtext_a11y_3: The thinking indicator is announced as "The assistant is thinking".
doc.streamingtext_choice_loader: While waiting for the first chunk of data (before streaming begins).
doc.streamingtext_choice_markdown: Static content that doesn't need to be streamed.
doc.streamingtext_choice_self: Real-time AI chat responses or live text updates.
doc.streamingtext_guideline_1: Ensure isStreaming is true while data is still being received.
doc.streamingtext_guideline_2: Use showThinking while waiting for the model to start responding.
doc.streamingtext_guideline_3: Avoid very high streaming speeds that may overwhelm the user's ability to read.
doc.streamingtext_intro: StreamingText renders text content with a dynamic "typing" effect, simulating the real-time generation characteristic of large language models. It supports Markdown rendering and can display a "thinking" indicator when generation is pending.
doc.streamingtext_kb_desc: As this is a read-only component, standard keyboard navigation for text and links applies.
doc.streamingtext_motion_desc: New characters appear with a subtle opacity fade. The "thinking" dots use a gentle pulse animation.
doc.streamingtext_practice_1: Provide a "Stop" button in the parent component to let users cancel long streams.
doc.streamingtext_practice_2: Ensure the background contrast is sufficient for reading the streaming text.
doc.streamingtext_practice_3: Use a monospaced font if the stream contains code or data tables.
doc.streamingtext_responsive: The text flows and wraps according to its container width. Scroll management ensures the latest content remains visible on small screens.
doc.streamingtext_scenario_1: Chatbot interface where responses appear word-by-word.
doc.streamingtext_scenario_2: Code generation tool showing snippets as they are written.
doc.streamingtext_scenario_3: Live transcriptions of audio or speech.
doc.terminal_a11y_1: The output body has role=log and aria-live=polite so screen readers announce new lines.
doc.terminal_a11y_3: Copy and Clear buttons carry descriptive aria-label attributes.
doc.terminal_choice_agent: Agent command execution and live output
doc.terminal_choice_error: Error output or process exit messages
doc.terminal_choice_thought: AI reasoning steps with status indicators
doc.terminal_content_guidelines_1: Use `type="input"` for commands, `type="output"` for stdout, `type="error"` for stderr, and `type="info"` for status messages to get correct color coding.
doc.terminal_content_guidelines_2: Provide a `title` that names the running process (e.g., `npm install`) so users immediately know what is executing.
doc.terminal_design_intent: Terminal provides a familiar developer UI for surfacing what an AI agent is doing under the hood. The macOS-style chrome signals this is a terminal at a glance without requiring users to parse a wall of text.
doc.terminal_i18n_desc: Copy and Clear button aria-labels are sourced from the `form` namespace (`terminal.copy_label`, `terminal.copied_label`, `terminal.clear_label`).
doc.terminal_intro: Terminal renders command input, output, errors, and info lines in a dark monospace window. It supports ANSI SGR color codes, auto-scroll to the latest output, and optional copy/clear actions.
doc.terminal_kb_tab: Move focus between Copy and Clear buttons.
doc.terminal_motion_desc: Auto-scroll jumps immediately to the latest line with no animation, minimizing perceived latency during agentic sessions.
doc.terminal_practice_1: Keep `autoScroll` enabled while the agent is running; disable it if the user scrolls up to inspect earlier output.
doc.terminal_practice_2: Set an explicit `height` to cap vertical growth when embedding the terminal in a constrained layout.
doc.terminal_responsive: The terminal fills its container width and scrolls horizontally for long lines. Set an explicit `height` to cap vertical growth in constrained layouts.
doc.terminal_scenario_1_desc: Streaming shell output from an AI agent building a project or running tests.
doc.terminal_scenario_2_desc: Displaying build and deploy steps in a CI/CD workflow embedded in a developer dashboard.
doc.thoughtprocess_a11y: The container uses role='region' with an aria-label. Individual steps are announced as they complete.
doc.thoughtprocess_a11y_1: The container has role="region" with an accessible name.
doc.thoughtprocess_a11y_3: Status changes are announced via aria-live in the parent if critical.
doc.thoughtprocess_best_practice_1: Collapse completed processes by default in long conversations to keep the UI clean.
doc.thoughtprocess_best_practice_2: Use the error status clearly to identify which specific step in a chain failed.
doc.thoughtprocess_choice_self: Complex multi-step AI tasks or agent reasoning.
doc.thoughtprocess_choice_timeline: General historical events or logs unrelated to AI reasoning.
doc.thoughtprocess_choice_transparency: Use when users need to see the internal steps of an AI agent to build trust or for debugging.
doc.thoughtprocess_choice_wait: Use to manage user expectations during long-running tasks by showing active progress.
doc.thoughtprocess_content_guidelines: Keep step descriptions short and actionable. Use the children area for detailed logs or terminal output.
doc.thoughtprocess_design_intent: Transparency in AI reasoning builds user confidence and aids in debugging. ThoughtProcess provides a standardized way to show the progress of background tasks, distinguishing between the high-level goal and individual execution steps.
doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_1: Use title to describe the overall goal (e.g., "Analyzing data...").
doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_2: Update ThoughtStep statuses in real-time as steps complete.
doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_3: Provide meaningful children content for steps to explain what happened in that phase.
doc.thoughtprocess_i18n: Status labels (Thinking, Completed, Error) are localized. Custom step titles are provided by the consumer.
doc.thoughtprocess_i18n_desc: Status labels and screen reader announcements are localized via the form namespace.
doc.thoughtprocess_intro: ThoughtProcess visualizes the "reasoning" steps of an AI agent or complex chain-of-thought process. It uses a timeline-style list of steps, each with its own status (pending, completed, or error), and can be collapsed to save space.
doc.thoughtprocess_kb_focus: Move focus through the toggle and any interactive links within steps.
doc.thoughtprocess_keyboard: Enter or Space on a step header toggles its expanded state. Tab moves between steps.
doc.thoughtprocess_motion: Steps expand and collapse with a smooth accordion-style animation. Status icons pulse when active.
doc.thoughtprocess_motion_desc: Expansion uses CSS transitions on the height and opacity. Status icons animate into view when changed.
doc.thoughtprocess_practice_1: Default to collapsed if the process is long and has already completed.
doc.thoughtprocess_practice_2: Use the 'error' status to highlight exactly where a chain failed.
doc.thoughtprocess_practice_3: Avoid too many steps (>10); group related sub-tasks if necessary.
doc.thoughtprocess_responsive: The timeline layout wraps and scales to fit the container width. The toggle button remains accessible on touch devices.
doc.thoughtprocess_scenario_1: Agentic workflows: Showing a multi-step plan before execution.
doc.thoughtprocess_scenario_2: Code execution: Listing steps like "Spinning up environment", "Running script", "Cleaning up".
doc.thoughtprocess_scenarios: Common in multi-agent workflows, code execution pipelines, or complex RAG retrieval steps.
doc.threadlist_a11y_1: The list is wrapped in a nav landmark with an accessible label so screen-reader users can jump to history.
doc.threadlist_a11y_2: The active thread is marked with aria-current so its selected state is announced.
doc.threadlist_a11y_3: Each delete button has its own aria-label so its purpose is clear out of context.
doc.threadlist_choice_list: A generic list of items without conversation semantics
doc.threadlist_choice_self: A conversation-history sidebar with previews and deletion
doc.threadlist_choice_sidebar: The surrounding collapsible app navigation shell
doc.threadlist_content_guidelines_1: Derive titles from the first user message and truncate to a single line; show a short preview below.
doc.threadlist_content_guidelines_2: Use relative timestamps (2m, 1h, 1d) so recency reads faster than absolute dates.
doc.threadlist_design_intent: Chat history is a navigation surface first. ThreadList keeps titles, previews, and timestamps legible at a glance and reveals destructive actions only on hover or focus.
doc.threadlist_i18n_desc: The new-conversation, empty, and delete labels are overridable through the labels prop; thread content comes from your data.
doc.threadlist_intro: ThreadList renders a conversation-history sidebar for AI chat apps — a scrollable list of past threads with an optional new-conversation action and per-thread deletion.
doc.threadlist_kb_activate: Open the focused thread or trigger its action
doc.threadlist_kb_tab: Move between threads and their delete buttons
doc.threadlist_motion_desc: Rows use a quick background-color transition on hover and focus; the delete button fades in rather than shifting layout.
doc.threadlist_practice_1: Confirm deletion for threads with meaningful content to avoid accidental loss.
doc.threadlist_practice_2: Keep the active thread visible when the list scrolls, and highlight it clearly.
doc.threadlist_practice_3: Group or paginate very long histories rather than rendering thousands of rows at once.
doc.threadlist_responsive: The list fills the width of its container, making it equally at home in a fixed sidebar or a full-width mobile drawer.
doc.threadlist_scenario_1_desc: A persistent left rail listing every conversation, with a new-chat button pinned at the top.
doc.threadlist_scenario_2_desc: Rendered inside a Drawer that slides in over the chat on small screens.
doc.usagemeter_a11y_1: The component uses role="meter" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax.
doc.usagemeter_a11y_2: An accessible label describes the used and maximum values for screen readers even when the bar is hidden.
doc.usagemeter_a11y_3: Warning and danger states are conveyed by the readout value, not by color alone.
doc.usagemeter_choice_self: Showing token usage against a context or quota limit
doc.usagemeter_choice_stats: A static metric tile without a budget or limit
doc.usagemeter_content_guidelines_1: Show both the used and maximum values so the remaining headroom is obvious; offer a percentage as an alternative readout.
doc.usagemeter_content_guidelines_2: Format large counts with thousands separators so 128000 reads as 128,000.
doc.usagemeter_design_intent: Token budgets are invisible until they are exceeded. UsageMeter makes headroom continuously visible and uses color to warn before a request is truncated or rejected.
doc.usagemeter_i18n_desc: The label and unit text are overridable through the labels prop; numeric formatting uses grouped thousands independent of locale.
doc.usagemeter_intro: UsageMeter (also exported as TokenCounter) visualizes token consumption against a budget such as a model's context window — a labeled bar plus a numeric readout that shifts to warning and danger colors near the limit.
doc.usagemeter_kb_desc: UsageMeter is a read-only status display and is not itself focusable or interactive.
doc.usagemeter_motion_desc: The bar animates its width and color as usage changes, so approaching the limit reads as motion, not just a static number.
doc.usagemeter_practice_1: Set warn and danger thresholds that match the real cost of overflowing, not arbitrary round numbers.
doc.usagemeter_practice_2: Update the value as tokens stream in so the meter reflects live consumption.
doc.usagemeter_practice_3: Drop the bar and keep the counter alone when there is no meaningful maximum to measure against.
doc.usagemeter_responsive: The meter fills the width of its container and the readout uses tabular figures so numbers stay aligned as they change.
doc.usagemeter_scenario_1_desc: Shown under a prompt input to track how much of the context window the current conversation consumes.
doc.usagemeter_scenario_2_desc: Displayed in a billing panel to show monthly token usage against the plan allowance.
doc.voicevisualizer_a11y_1: Provide an ariaLabel summarizing the audio (e.g. "Recording in progress"); without one, the visualizer is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so adjacent text carries the meaning.
doc.voicevisualizer_a11y_2: Use isActive=false to apply reduced opacity when the visualizer is not capturing audio — this prevents users from thinking audio is active when it is not.
doc.voicevisualizer_choice_self: Visualize microphone or audio playback levels
doc.voicevisualizer_content_guidelines_1: For bars mode, normalize data from `AnalyserNode.getByteFrequencyData()` (0–255) by dividing by 255 before passing.
doc.voicevisualizer_content_guidelines_2: For waveform mode, use `AnalyserNode.getByteTimeDomainData()` (0–255) and normalize by dividing by 255. Silence = 0.5.
doc.voicevisualizer_design_intent: Voice interfaces need a visual confirmation that audio is being captured and processed. VoiceVisualizer provides this without requiring any Canvas code or audio setup — the consumer feeds normalized data and the component handles all rendering.
doc.voicevisualizer_i18n_desc: This component contains no text content. No i18n configuration is required.
doc.voicevisualizer_intro: VoiceVisualizer renders an SVG audio-level indicator in two styles: animated bars or a smooth waveform. It accepts live amplitude data from the Web Audio API AnalyserNode (normalized 0–1), and falls back to a looping idle animation when no data is provided.
doc.voicevisualizer_kb_tab: The SVG is not keyboard-focusable. Without ariaLabel it is aria-hidden; with one it is an image and still not in the tab order.
doc.voicevisualizer_motion_desc: Bars animate with a staggered scale-Y pulse during idle; the waveform scrolls horizontally. Data-driven updates use CSS transitions for smooth height changes. Animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
doc.voicevisualizer_practice_1: Drive the component with `requestAnimationFrame` to keep data in sync with the audio buffer (~60 fps).
doc.voicevisualizer_practice_2: Set `isActive={false}` when the audio context is paused or the mic permission is not granted.
doc.voicevisualizer_responsive: VoiceVisualizer uses `width=100%` so it fills its container naturally. Control size via the parent container width and the `height` prop.
doc.voicevisualizer_scenario_1_desc: Display the microphone level while a user is speaking to an AI assistant, confirming the voice is being captured.
doc.voicevisualizer_scenario_2_desc: Show frequency bars during TTS output to give visual feedback while the AI is speaking.
